solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Applications for injury benefit, perhaps

parts.note: reads like claim forms for a state injury allowance, but means things applied to a wound to do it good

explanation.surface: Someone filling in forms to claim state benefit after getting hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Applications' and 'benefit' suggest welfare paperwork; here they are things you apply to a cut, which benefit it by stopping infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Germ-killing lotions are applied to wounds and cuts to help them heal cleanly.

clue.text: Garble a broadcast that discovers unknowns

indicators.note: seeds broadcast are scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A garbled radio broadcast that somehow reveals secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scatters GARBLE into ALGEBR, and the A that follows stays where it is, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of mathematics uses symbols such as x and y to solve for unknown quantities.

clue.text: The herb season, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a season is a period or time of year

explanation.surface: Someone remarking that it is the season for a particular herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns TIME (season) into a word pronounced the same but spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant culinary plant of the mint family used for seasoning.

clue.text: Gems you can safely handle

definitions.meaning: diamonds and other jewels are informally called sparkling stones or rocks
hand-held fireworks waved about on Bonfire Night

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for diamonds, and also the hand-held fireworks that fizz with sparks when held at arm's length.

clue.text: Weapon for spearing fish?

definitions.meaning: a long infantry spear with a pointed steel head
a predatory freshwater fish with a long snout

explanation.definitionFit: A long-shafted infantry spear, and also a large predatory freshwater fish.

clue.text: Animated spider in webbing

indicators.note: weaving a web works strands into a new pattern, so the letters are woven into a new order

explanation.surface: A lively spider at work in its web.
explanation.walkthrough: 'webbing' rearranges SPIDER plus IN; 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone filled with lively creative spirit is said to be stimulated or roused.

clue.text: Flapping sails of hemp fibre

indicators.note: sails flapping in the wind are tossed about, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Sails made of hemp flapping in the breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flapping' rearranges SAILS; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough fibre from an agave plant, used like hemp to make rope and twine.

clue.text: Multiply without going forth

parts.note: breeding without going out of the family, an echo of the biblical 'go forth and multiply'

explanation.surface: A twist on the biblical command to go forth and multiply.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis tells humanity to 'be fruitful and multiply'; breeding that stays within a closed group instead of going outside is the sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: Mating closely related animals breeds within a limited family line rather than outside it.

clue.text: Illegally dispatched

parts.note: dispatched in the sense of killed, done so unlawfully

explanation.surface: Something sent off by post without authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatched' suggests sending a parcel; here it means killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlawful killing of a person is the crime of homicide with intent.

clue.text: Chap soundly digs his plot, he's remembered today

parts.note: guy is an informal word for a man or chap

indicators.note: taken by sound, so the word is pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: forks as a verb means digs with a garden fork

explanation.surface: A man busily digging over his garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' turns FORKS (digs) into a name pronounced the same in non-rhotic British speech. 'his plot' points to the 1605 Gunpowder Plot; he is burnt in effigy on Bonfire Night, 5 November.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gunpowder Plot conspirator is commemorated every 5 November with bonfires and fireworks.

clue.text: If damp it's unlikely to make much impact

definitions.text: If damp it's unlikely to make much impact

parts.words: If damp it's unlikely to make much impact
parts.note: plays on the phrase for a disappointing anticlimax: a small firework that fizzles when wet

explanation.surface: A general observation about things that fail to impress.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'damp squib' is the idiom for a letdown; a small firework that has got wet fails to go off.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hissing firework, which fizzles out if it has got wet, hence the idiom for an anticlimax.

clue.text: Turning balls that may offer chances

definitions.meaning: in cricket, deliveries that deviate off the pitch
opportunities or lucky openings, as in 'give me a break'

explanation.definitionFit: Cricket balls that deviate sharply after pitching, and lucky opportunities in everyday speech.

clue.text: Dogs, idle in disposition, will be put out

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Idle dogs are evicted from their spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disposition' rearranges DOGS and IDLE; 'will be' links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To force something or someone out of an established position is to oust or remove them.

clue.text: Goes easy — Mabel's upset

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes things gently because Mabel is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges MABELS, the S of the possessive counting as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Walks at a slow, relaxed pace, the sense of strolling.

clue.text: Pretentious person turns up, about to light tonight's conflagrations

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other
in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a snob is a person who looks down on others pretentiously
to light is to set on fire

explanation.surface: A snob turns up at a party, ready to set the evening's blazes going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses the snob, giving BONS, and 'about' wraps that round the light; 'to' is a link word. Bonfire Night is 5 November in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Large outdoor fires, lit across Britain on 5 November, Guy Fawkes Night.

clue.text: Certainly in drink — so restrained

indicators.note: one word is placed in the other

parts.note: mead is an alcoholic drink made from honey
sure is used to mean certainly, as in 'sure, I'll come'

explanation.surface: A drinker insists they are definitely sober and self-controlled.
explanation.definitionFit: Measured speech or behaviour is careful, controlled and deliberate.

clue.text: Propose a funny article following serial drama

indicators.note: following means coming after, placing this piece at the end
funny means odd, so the letters are made odd by rearrangement

parts.note: a is the indefinite article in grammar

explanation.surface: A marriage proposal in a television serial, played for laughs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges the first two words; 'following' puts the article after them. Soap operas got the name from the detergent firms that sponsored early radio serials.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running radio or television serial about everyday lives, originally sponsored by detergent makers.

clue.text: Star of the Magic Circle?

parts.note: sounds like a leading conjuror of the famous magicians' society, but means a five-pointed star figure drawn inside a ring for occult use

explanation.surface: The headline performer at the Magic Circle, Britain's society of conjurors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is a London club for stage magicians; the star meant here is a geometric symbol used in ritual magic.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed star symbol, often within a circle, used as a magic or occult emblem.

clue.text: Is he going in to discover it's all over?

indicators.note: going in means entering, so these letters are placed inside the other word

parts.note: to discover something is to find it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether he is going inside to learn the game is up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going in' puts IS HE inside FIND; 'to' and 'it's' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is complete or ended, it is said to be over and done with.

clue.text: Slip, perhaps, if up tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
the elder is a small tree with white flowers and dark berries

explanation.surface: Someone slips while climbing a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives FI (IF reversed). Slip is a cricket position close to the batsman, so a player there is one example; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer stationed in a fielding position such as slip, so slip is one example.

clue.text: Roman sort of light providing sparks

definitions.text: Roman sort of light providing sparks

parts.words: Roman sort of light providing sparks
parts.note: a Roman-named firework tube that shoots out balls of fire, built on a word for a wax light

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman lamp throwing off sparks.
explanation.walkthrough: A Roman candle is a firework; 'Roman' looks historical but completes the firework's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax stick with a wick that gives light, also part of the name of a sparking firework.

clue.text: Values seem set for a change

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone's values appear fixed, but are due for a shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges SEEM SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Holds in high regard or respect, as one prizes something.

clue.text: Move to a new country home

definitions.text: Move to a new country home

parts.words: Move to a new country home
parts.note: reads like relocating to a rural house, but means making one's home in a different nation

explanation.surface: Someone relocating to a new house in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country home' suggests a rural house; read it as setting up home in another country.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave one's homeland and settle permanently in another nation.

clue.text: With revision tries to take the examination again

indicators.note: revision means altering, so the letters are revised into a new order

explanation.surface: A student revises hard and tries the exam a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With revision' rearranges TRIES; revision also fits the exam setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A student who failed sits the same test a second time.

clue.text: Firework lecture

definitions.meaning: a firework propelled skyward on a stick
British informal for a sharp reprimand or telling-off

explanation.definitionFit: A firework that shoots skyward, and in British slang a severe telling-off.

clue.text: Combination of metals used in common tool

parts.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: An everyday tool is made from an alloy of metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combination of' joins three chemical symbols, all metals, as a charade; 'used in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting blade with a handle is among the most everyday of implements.

clue.text: A highlight of the night that's clear

definitions.text: A highlight of the night that's clear

parts.words: A highlight of the night that's clear
parts.note: reads like the best moment of an evening, but means a bright point visible in a cloudless night sky

explanation.surface: Someone recalling the best moment of a fine evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highlight' suggests the best part of an event; literally it is a point of light seen when the sky is clear.
explanation.definitionFit: A distant sun appears as a bright point in the sky on a cloudless night.

clue.text: Clothes in season

definitions.meaning: to add a sauce or flavouring, as one does to a salad

explanation.definitionFit: Garments worn on the body, and to add oil or sauce to food such as a salad.

clue.text: She may take the wheel with dazzling effect

definitions.text: She may take the wheel with dazzling effect

parts.words: She may take the wheel with dazzling effect
parts.note: reads like a woman driving, but points to the spinning firework named after a saint martyred on a wheel

explanation.surface: A woman driver dazzling onlookers behind the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: A Catherine wheel is a spinning firework, named after St Catherine of Alexandria, who was sentenced to die on a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, and the first word of the pinwheel firework that spins in a dazzling circle.

clue.text: The Services may prove decisive in these struggles

definitions.text: The Services may prove decisive in these struggles

parts.words: The Services may prove decisive in these struggles
parts.note: reads like the armed forces winning battles, but means tennis serves deciding extra games played to settle a level set

explanation.surface: The armed forces could tip the balance in a conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Services' suggests the army, navy and air force; in tennis, holding serve is key in the extra game that settles a set at six-all.
explanation.definitionFit: Deciding games played when a set or match is level, as in tennis at six games all.
